result.text:
I couldn't pin or run anything yet. The working directory (`/tmp/fred-eval/.../P07/ws`) has only the `.claude/skills/` files. There's no `application.fam`, no app source and no existing `.ufbt*` state, and I have no shell in this session. So the build is **`blocked`**, not `pass`: there is no project to build and no toolchain to build with.

## How to pin it

Do this from your app directory, the one containing `application.fam`. Two points first:

- **Read `application.fam` and any build hooks before building.** The manifest is Python that the build runs.
- **The download only happens if you approve it.** The first `ufbt update` fetches the SDK and toolchain from the internet. Without a pin, uFBT bootstraps from the moving `release` channel.

```bash
# 1. Keep the SDK in a project-local folder so your global ~/.ufbt is untouched
export UFBT_HOME="$PWD/.ufbt-1.5.1"

# 2. Download the exact SDK archive and check its hash before using it
curl -fLo flipper-z-f7-sdk-1.5.1.zip \
  https://update.flipperzero.one/builds/firmware/1.5.1/flipper-z-f7-sdk-1.5.1.zip
echo "dfde39df32ba8a9789b26afc1d702579ad8399a1c285770637cfe3287b2e2ffe  flipper-z-f7-sdk-1.5.1.zip" | sha256sum -c -

# 3. Install that file (only if step 2 printed OK)
ufbt update --local=flipper-z-f7-sdk-1.5.1.zip

# 4. Delete any old dist/ so nothing stale gets reported as fresh, then build
rm -rf dist && ufbt
sha256sum dist/*.fap
```

Using `--local` with a hash-checked file is stricter than `ufbt update --branch=1.5.1`, which works too but trusts whatever the server returns. One caveat: the URL and hash come from Flipper's live update index (checked 2026-10-16). Nobody has hashed the actual downloaded bytes yet, which is what step 2 does.

Write down these values so the result means something: uFBT version, SDK URL and hash, API version (it should be **88.2**), firmware commit (`9e810dc399e027e48ce07751df72168abbb19065`), compiler version, your app's commit, and the `.fap` hash.

## What a clean build proves

- Your C code compiles and links against the 1.5.1 f7 SDK headers and libraries.
- Every function it calls is exported in the API 88.2 table, so the loader shouldn't reject it for a missing symbol on 1.5.1.
- The manifest is accepted by the build.
- `dist/` contains a `.fap` with a known hash, built from known inputs.

## What it doesn't prove

- **That the app works on a Flipper.** It says nothing about drawing, input handling, exit and cleanup, timers and worker threads, storage I/O, memory use or crashes. Only running on a real device shows those.
- **Logic correctness.** That needs host tests of the extracted logic, and there is no `ufbt test`.
- **Radio, GPIO, IR, NFC or electrical behaviour.**
- **Compatibility with other firmware.** It covers official 1.5.1 / API 88.2 only. Momentum, Unleashed and later official versions each need their own build and device check.
- **Reproducibility.** Getting the same `.fap` hash every time requires comparing two clean builds.
- **Catalog acceptance.** The catalog has its own manifest, screenshot and license checks.
- **Code quality.** `ufbt lint` (if you run it) only checks formatting and naming. It is not static analysis.

## Status right now

| Check | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| SDK pinned | blocked | No project here; the download needs your go-ahead |
| SDK archive hash checked | not-run | Not downloaded yet |
| Compiled | blocked | No `application.fam` or toolchain |
| Host tests | not-run | No source |
| Behaviour on a device | not-run | Needs hardware, and you'd have to approve that separately |

To have me run it, open the session in the app's repo and confirm the SDK and toolchain download. I'll then run the steps above and fill in a validation report with the exact commands, exit codes and hashes.
